pairs: Congregantes autem Philisthiim agmina sua in prælium,
Now the Philistines, gathering their troops for battle,
et castrametati sunt inter Socho et Azeca in finibus Dommim.
And they made camp between Socoh and Azekah, within the borders of Dammim.
Porro Saul et filii Israël congregati venerunt in Vallem terebinthi,
But Saul and the sons of Israel, having gathered together, went to the Valley of Terebinth.
et direxerunt aciem ad pugnandum contra Philisthiim.
And they positioned the army so as to fight against the Philistines.
Et Philisthiim stabant super montem ex parte hac,
And the Philistines were standing on a mountain on the one side,
et Israël stabat supra montem ex altera parte:
and Israel was standing on a mountain on the other side.
And there was a valley between them.
Et egressus est vir spurius de castris Philisthinorum nomine Goliath,
And there went out from the camp of the Philistines,
whose height was six cubits and a palm.
et cassis ærea super caput ejus,
And he had a helmet of brass upon his head,
and he was clothed with a breastplate of scales.
the weight of his breastplate was five thousand shekels of brass.
et ocreas æreas habebat in cruribus,
And he had plates of brass on his lower legs,
et clypeus æreus tegebat humeros ejus.
and a small shield of brass was covering his shoulders.
Hastile autem hastæ ejus erat quasi liciatorium texentium:
Now the shaft of his spear was like the beam used by a weaver.
ipsum autem ferrum hastæ ejus sexcentos siclos habebat ferri:
And the iron of his spear held six hundred shekels of iron.
And his armor bearer went before him.
And standing still, he cried out to the battle lines of Israel,
“Why have you arrived, prepared for battle?
numquid ego non sum Philisthæus, et vos servi Saul?
Am I not a Philistine, and are you not the servants of Saul?
Choose one man from among you,
and let him descend to do battle alone.
If he is able to fight with me
But if I will prevail over him,
“I have reproached the troops of Israel today.
and let him undertake a fight against me alone.”
Audiens autem Saul et omnes Israëlitæ sermones Philisthæi hujuscemodi,
And Saul and all the Israelites,
hearing these words of the Philistine in this manner,
David autem erat filius viri Ephrathæi,
Now David was the son of an Ephrathite man,
et erat vir in diebus Saul senex,
and during the days of Saul, he was an elderly man,
and of great age among men.
Abierunt autem tres filii ejus majores post Saul in prælium:
Now his three eldest sons followed Saul into battle.
et nomina trium filiorum ejus qui perrexerunt ad bellum,
And the names of his three sons, who went to the battle,
Therefore, when the three eldest had followed Saul,
et reversus est a Saul ut pasceret gregem patris sui in Bethlehem.
and he returned, so that he might pasture the flock of his father at Bethlehem.
Procedebat vero Philisthæus mane et vespere,
Truly, the Philistine advanced morning and evening,
and he stood forth, for forty days.
Dixit autem Isai ad David filium suum:
Now Jesse said to his son David: “Take,
for your brothers, an ephah of cooked grain,
et curre in castra ad fratres tuos,
and hurry to the camp, to your brothers.
et decem formellas casei has deferes ad tribunum:
And you shall carry these ten little cheeses to the tribune.
et fratres tuos visitabis, si recte agant:
And visit your brothers, to see if they are doing well.
et cum quibus ordinati sunt, disce.
And learn with whom they have been stationed.”
But they were in the valley of Terebinth,
and all the sons of Israel,
in Valle terebinthi pugnabant adversum Philisthiim.
And so, David rose up in the morning,
and he commended the flock to the caretaker.
just as Jesse had instructed him.
And he went to the place of the battle line,
qui egressus ad pugnam vociferatus erat in certamine.
in going out to fight, was shouting in the conflict.
For Israel had positioned their troops,
sed et Philisthiim ex adverso fuerant præparati.
but the Philistines also had prepared themselves against them.
Derelinquens ergo David vasa quæ attulerat sub manu custodis ad sarcinas,
Then, leaving the items that he had brought under the hand of the keeper of baggage,
David ran to the place of the conflict.
et interrogabat si omnia recte agerentur erga fratres suos.
And he was asking if all was going well with his brothers.
And while he was still speaking with them,
there appeared the man of spurious descent,
ascending from the camp of the Philistines.
et loquente eo hæc eadem verba audivit David.
And he was speaking in these same words, which David heard.
when they had seen the man,
Et dixit unus quispiam de Israël:
For he ascended in order to reproach Israel.
Therefore, the man who will strike him down,
the king will enrich with great wealth,
and will give to him his daughter,
et domum patris ejus faciet absque tributo in Israël.
and will cause his father’s house to be free of tribute in Israel.”
Et ait David ad viros qui stabant secum,
And David spoke to the men who were standing with him,
Quid dabitur viro qui percusserit Philisthæum hunc,
“What will be given to the man who will have struck down this Philistine,
and who will have taken away the disgrace from Israel?
quis enim est hic Philisthæus incircumcisus,
For who is this uncircumcised Philistine,
that he should reproach the soldiers of the living God?”
Referebat autem ei populus eumdem sermonem,
Then the people repeated to him the same words,
Hæc dabuntur viro qui percusserit eum.
“These things shall be given to the man who will have struck him down.”
Quod cum audisset Eliab frater ejus major,
as he was speaking with the others,
et quare dereliquisti pauculas oves illas in deserto?
And why did you leave behind those few sheep in the wilderness?
I know your pride and the wickedness of your heart,
that you have come down so that you might see the battle.”
Is there any word against me?”
Et declinavit paululum ab eo ad alium:
And he turned away from him a little, toward another.
And he asked the same question.
Et respondit ei populus verbum sicut prius.
And the people responded to him as before.
Audita sunt autem verba quæ locutus est David,
Now the words that David had spoken were heard
and reported in the sight of Saul.
When he had been led to Saul,
Non concidat cor cujusquam in eo:
“Let no one lose heart over him. I,
ego servus tuus vadam, et pugnabo adversus Philisthæum.
your servant, shall go and fight against the Philistine.”
“You are not able to withstand this Philistine,
hic autem vir bellator est ab adolescentia sua.
but he has been a warrior from his boyhood.”
Pascebat servus tuus patris sui gregem,
“Your servant was pasturing the flock of his father.
And there approached a lion or a bear,
et tollebat arietem de medio gregis:
and it took a ram from the midst of the flock.
and I rescued from their mouth.
And they rose up against me.
And I caught them by the throat,
et ursum interfeci ego servus tuus:
have killed both lion and bear.
et Philisthæus hic incircumcisus quasi unus ex eis.
will be like one of them.
Now I will go and take away the reproach of the people.
quoniam quis est iste Philisthæus incircumcisus,
For who is this uncircumcised Philistine,
qui ausus est maledicere exercitui Dei viventis?
who has dared to curse the army of the living God?”
Dominus qui eripuit me de manu leonis,
“The Lord who rescued me from the hand of the lion,
and from the hand of the bear,
ipse me liberabit de manu Philisthæi hujus.
he himself will free me from the hand of this Philistine.”
and may the Lord be with you.”
Et induit Saul David vestimentis suis,
And Saul clothed David with his garments.
et imposuit galeam æream super caput ejus,
And he placed a helmet of brass upon his head,
and he clothed him with a breastplate.
Accinctus ergo David gladio ejus super vestem suam,
Then David, having girded his sword over his armor,
cœpit tentare si armatus posset incedere:
began to see if he could walk in the armor.
But he was not accustomed to it.
“I cannot move about in this way.
For I am not used to it.”
And he took up his staff,
which he held always in his hands.
et elegit sibi quinque limpidissimos lapides de torrente,
And he chose for himself five very smooth stones from the torrent.
et misit eos in peram pastoralem quam habebat secum,
And he put them into the shepherd’s bag that he had with him.
And he took up a sling in his hand.
And he went out against the Philistine.
went and drew near against David.
And his armor bearer was before him.
And when the Philistine had seen
And the Philistine said to David,
quod tu venis ad me cum baculo?
that you approach against me with a staff?”
Et maledixit Philisthæus David in diis suis:
And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
et dabo carnes tuas volatilibus cæli
and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air,
and to the beasts of the earth.”
But David said to the Philistine:
Tu venis ad me cum gladio,
ego autem venio ad te in nomine Domini exercituum,
But I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts,
the God of the armies of Israel, which you have reproached.
et dabit te Dominus in manu mea,
the Lord will deliver you into my hand,
and I will strike you down.
et auferam caput tuum a te:
And I will take your head from you.
et dabo cadavera castrorum Philisthiim hodie volatilibus cæli,
And today, I will give the carcasses of the camp of the Philistines to the birds of the air,
et bestiis terræ, ut sciat omnis terra quia est Deus in Israël,
and to the beasts of the earth, so that all the earth may know that God is with Israel.
And this entire assembly will know that the Lord does not save by sword,
quia non in gladio nec in hasta salvat Dominus:
et tradet vos in manus nostras.
and he will deliver you into our hands.”
when the Philistine had risen up,
and was drawing near against David,
et cucurrit ad pugnam ex adverso Philisthæi.
David hurried and ran to the fight against the Philistine.
Et misit manum suam in peram,
And he put his hand into his bag,
tulitque unum lapidem, et funda jecit,
and took out one stone. And swinging it around,
et circumducens percussit Philisthæum in fronte:
he cast it with the sling and struck the Philistine on the forehead.
et infixus est lapis in fronte ejus,
And the stone became imbedded in his forehead.
et cecidit in faciem suam super terram.
And he fell on his face, upon the ground.
Prævaluitque David adversum Philisthæum in funda et lapide,
And David prevailed against the Philistine with a sling and a stone.
And he struck and killed the Philistine.
Cumque gladium non haberet in manu David,
But since David held no sword in his hand,
he ran and stood over the Philistine,
et eduxit eum de vagina sua:
and withdrew it from the sheath.
et interfecit eum, præciditque caput ejus.
And he killed him and cut off his head.
Videntes autem Philisthiim quod mortuus esset fortissimus eorum,
Then the Philistines, seeing that their strongest man was dead,
And the men of Israel and Judah,
et persecuti sunt Philisthæos usque dum venirent in vallem,
shouted and pursued after the Philistines,
even until they arrived at the valley and as far as the gates of Ekron.
cecideruntque vulnerati de Philisthiim in via Saraim,
And many wounded among the Philistines fell on the way of Shaaraim,
Et revertentes filii Israël postquam persecuti fuerant Philisthæos,
And the sons of Israel, returning after they had pursued the Philistines,
Then David, taking up the head of the Philistine,
arma vero ejus posuit in tabernaculo suo.
Yet truly, he placed his armor in his own tent.
Eo autem tempore quo viderat Saul David egredientem contra Philisthæum,
Now at the time that Saul had seen David going out against the Philistines,
he said to Abner, the leader of the military,
De qua stirpe descendit hic adolescens,
“From what stock is this youth descended,
Interroga tu, cujus filius sit iste puer.
“You shall inquire as to whose son this boy may be.”
after the Philistine had been struck down,
having the head of the Philistine in his hand.
Filius servi tui Isai Bethlehemitæ ego sum.
“I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem.”
